label: has equivalent effect as
type: the subject statement/action produces the same end result as the object statement, action, or sequence of statements, even though the surface mechanism differs (one statement vs. a sequence, a DDL statement vs. a UI action). Distinct from isSynonymOf (two names for one thing) and from mustUseInsteadWhen (a required substitution) - this predicate is for two DIFFERENT mechanisms that a page explicitly states reach the same outcome.
evidence: This is equivalent to running CREATE ANALYTICS SCOPE followed by CREATE ANALYTICS COLLECTION.
This is equivalent to running DROP ANALYTICS COLLECTION, and if necessary DROP ANALYTICS SYNONYM.
relates_to_competency_question: Are two differently-shaped operations (a single statement vs. a sequence, a statement vs. a UI click) stated to produce the same result?
